video_title: Concurrency is about hiding latency, not making one core faster
core_insight: Concurrency overlaps waiting work so the system keeps making progress; parallelism uses multiple cores for CPU work. Choose async for I/O bound, threads/processes for CPU bound, and bound concurrency to stay predictable.

scenes.voice: Why does a single fast CPU still feel slow under load? The problem isn't compute, it's waiting.
scenes.visual: Single request timeline with long idle gaps on I/O, CPU utilization drops to zero during waits.

scenes.voice: One execution path can only do one thing at a time. When a request blocks on DB or network, the thread is wasted for tens of milliseconds.
scenes.visual: One thread timeline blocked on DB call, idle gap highlighted.

scenes.voice: The real constraint is latency hiding and resource utilization. We need progress on B while A is waiting.
scenes.visual: Two request timelines, A waiting, B starts in the gap.

scenes.voice: Concurrency is overlapping work, not necessarily simultaneous. Think of one chef with many orders, interleaving prep and waiting.
scenes.visual: Chef analogy with timers, chopping while simmering.

scenes.voice: Two families. Shared-memory with threads for CPU bound work, but shared state is dangerous. Cooperative event-driven with async await for I/O bound work, one thread, many tasks, never block the loop.
scenes.visual: Split screen: threads preemptive switching vs event loop with tasks yielding on I/O.

scenes.voice: The essential mechanism is the same: a scheduler, a way to yield, and a way to resume.
scenes.visual: Simple flow diagram of API to event loop to tasks.
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
    Client1 --> API[API Handler]
    Client2 --> API
    Client3 --> API
    API --> Loop[Event Loop]
    Loop --> TaskA[Task A waiting I/O]
    Loop --> TaskB[Task B CPU work]
    Loop --> TaskC[Task C waiting I/O]
    TaskA -- I/O complete --> Loop

scenes.voice: Choose async for I/O bound APIs and ingestion where most time is waiting. Choose threads or processes for CPU bound work like inference. Mixing both is normal.
scenes.visual: Payment service diagram: async API layer, bounded worker pool for fraud scoring, queue for events.

scenes.voice: Concurrency buys throughput at the cost of reasoning. Bound concurrency, avoid blocking the loop, and design for backpressure and observability from day one.
scenes.visual: Bounded pool with semaphore, backpressure signal, metrics.

mental_model: Think of concurrency as a chef interleaving orders: you cannot cook two dishes at once, but you can keep the kitchen busy by switching when one is waiting. Async hides I/O latency on one core; threads/processes use multiple cores for CPU work. Always bound concurrency and keep the hot path non-blocking.
final_takeaway: Concurrency hides latency, parallelism uses cores. Use async for I/O, threads for CPU, and bound your concurrency.
